summary: A concentration threshold written with an explicit '%' suffix must always be divided by 100, regardless of magnitude; the bare-number >1 heuristic must not be the only path to percent scaling.
reason: parseShareLimit stripped the '%' suffix before applying a 'v > 1 means percentage' heuristic, so any explicit percentage <= 1 (e.g. '1%', '0.5%') failed the guard and was returned as a fraction of 1.0 (a 100% threshold), silently disabling breach detection for ts concentration --limit. Capturing the '%' before stripping makes the suffix authoritative.
validated_outcome: Added hadPercent capture; '1%' -> 0.01 and '0.5%' -> 0.005 now correct, while '10', '10%', '0.1', '25 %' continue to parse as before (regression tests added).
